Zimbabwe’s Meditech Solutions Enters Liquidation Amid Financial Strains

HARARE, June 17—Meditech Solutions (Pvt) Ltd, a leading Zimbabwean manufacturer and distributor in the Medical Equipment & Devices sector, has entered liquidation after failing to overcome persistent financial difficulties, the company confirmed Monday. The move raises immediate questions about the future of its operations and workforce, with the process still unfolding.

A statement released by the company’s board said, “Despite extensive restructuring efforts and negotiations with creditors, Meditech Solutions is no longer able to meet its financial obligations. The board has therefore resolved to place the company into liquidation with effect from today.” The company, founded in 2003 and headquartered in Harare, is a prominent supplier of diagnostic imaging systems, surgical instruments and hospital monitoring devices within Zimbabwe.

Meditech Solutions employs approximately 120 staff across its production plant and administrative offices. Operations at its main factory in the Msasa industrial area have been suspended, with liquidation administrators appointed to oversee asset evaluation and creditor claims. Staff were notified Monday morning, and many could be seen leaving the premises carrying personal belongings.

Company spokesperson Lindiwe Chikore told reporters, “This is a difficult day for all of us. We are doing everything possible to ensure a fair process for employees and creditors.” She said the company’s hotline would remain open for staff queries during the transition period.

Industry analysts say Meditech Solutions’ collapse follows a prolonged period of foreign currency shortages, rising input costs, and reduced access to working capital. “Meditech’s financial distress reflects broader challenges in the medical devices sector, where currency volatility and limited local financing have made operations increasingly difficult,” said Tendai Mafusire, a Harare-based healthcare industry consultant.

The Zimbabwe Medical Devices Association said in a brief statement, “We regret the liquidation of Meditech Solutions and are monitoring the situation closely. We urge all stakeholders to prioritize the interests of workers and ensure an orderly winding down of operations.”

Liquidators have not yet announced a timetable for the sale of assets or potential redundancies. According to documents filed with the High Court of Zimbabwe, creditors are being asked to submit claims by the end of the month.

As the process continues, Meditech Solutions’ facilities remain under the control of the appointed liquidators, who are expected to provide further updates in the coming days.
